Hi Scott,

Thanks for the three photos, I opened all of them. IMG_0562 shows the BS-4 standing up with the water loop lit blue, IMG_0563 is the loose white plastic piece that came out of the box, and IMG_0564 shows the red selector on the power supply now reading 115.

On the voltage first, because that is the important one: 115 is the correct setting for a North American outlet, so what the switch reads in your photo is right. You did exactly the right thing catching it before plugging in. Good news is that the harmless direction is the one you had, a 115V supply switched to 230 on a 120V outlet simply will not come up properly, it is the opposite case (115 selected on a 230V mains) that damages things. So no hidden harm was done. Just double check the slider is seated fully on 115 and not sitting halfway, and leave it there.

On the broken piece, I cannot yet tell from the photo where it came from, and that is the one thing that decides whether the unit is fine to run. It looks like a small tab or clip rather than anything structural. Could you look the chassis over and send me one photo of the spot it broke off, plus a close up of the serial number label? While you have it in your hands, check two things: that nothing inside the frame is wet or sticky anywhere around the pump, radiator or the tubing joints, since this is a water cooled unit and a knock hard enough to snap plastic is the kind that can nip a fitting, and that the fans and the pump spin freely by hand with nothing rubbing.

If the break is a cosmetic trim or stand piece and everything is dry, it is safe to power the BS-4 up on 115 and start it hashing while we sort out the broken part. If anything is damp, or the piece turns out to be holding the radiator, pump or a fan in place, leave it unplugged and tell me, and we will treat it differently.

Send those photos over and I will take it from there with our hardware lead. If you prefer to talk it through live, our Discord is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi,

Here it is again.

[Image.jpeg]
Handed to the team · Frame part needed for a shipping-damaged BS-4; part decision is JD's, and the 23

Hi Scott,

That circle tells me what I needed. The piece that broke is the top of the diagonal rib on the white printed frame, the arm that runs up beside the fan and meets the top shell, and the fragment in your earlier photo matches that break exactly. Clean snap, typical of a knock in transit.

The good news is that it is frame only. In the same photo I can see the board sitting square on its standoffs, the Ethernet jack and USB-C port straight and undamaged, the fan still properly cap····its shroud and all the cabling intact, and you have reported nothing wet. That rib is a brace, not the part that carries the board or holds the fan, so the unit is electrically and mechanically sound and nothing about the break makes it unsafe to run.

So you can go ahead and power it up on 115 and let it hash. Before you do, give the board a gentle wiggle with a finger and do the same to the fan housing. Both should feel firm with no play and no rattle. Then stand the unit where it will live, keep it on a hard flat surface rather than carpet or a soft mat so the intake underneath stays clear, and watch the first few minutes: the fan should spin up immediately and the temperature on the UI should settle rather than climb. If you ever see the fan tilt or the board sag toward that corner, stop it and tell me, but I do not expect that from this break.

I have passed the whole thing with your photos to JD, our hardware lead, flagged as a frame part on Shop····, and I have also told the team the power supply arrived set to 230V on a US order so they can check the rest of that batch. A colleague is picking it up today and you will get the answer on the part in this thread.

If you want to talk it through live while you set it up, our Discord is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD is @nullhashrate there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

I also ordered the overclocking package and did not get anything extra.  Also the power kit/wall plug that shows actual power usage as well as the miner duster, neither have been delivered.

Thank you,
Scott
